label: D1 after an unrewarded trial, with a moderate lean toward a2
explanation: Fires only at D1 (100% of mass; never at GO or D2), and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (in_rew = 0 at D1: 98% of mass, rate 7.7% vs 0.2% after a reward). On those steps it fires when the agent leans moderately toward a2: the policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) at that D1 step is between about -6 and -1.5 (84% of mass is in the [-4.4, -1.5) choice bin, and there is none below -8.9 or above 8). It is also concentrated in a middle value band (7.1-7.5) and is silent at high value. Unrewarded D1 alone gives F1 0.37 (recall 0.95). Adding the upcoming action a2 gives F1 0.56. The recorded predicate uses the observed missing reward and the model's own logit at that step, with no future variables (dev P 0.55, R 0.88, F1 0.68, mass recall 0.90). Adding prev_common != 0 (the unrewarded trial had a common transition) raises precision to 0.75 but lowers recall to 0.63 at a similar F1 (0.69), so common-unrewarded trials make it fire more often and harder than rare-unrewarded ones. Activations are small (max 0.054). The top activations are at D1 right after an a2 choice that reached S2 by a common transition and went unrewarded, when the agent then repeats a2. It does not fire after rewarded trials or when the agent strongly prefers either action.
